items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline. Deadpan and dry on the joke lines.
lines: You could lose a war to a bird. Australia did.
But first... Australia is wider than the Moon.
Almost four thousand kilometres wide. The Moon? Three thousand four hundred and seventy-four.
And this giant won't sit still. It drifts seven centimetres every year.
So in twenty seventeen, Australia officially moved itself one point eight metres on the map.
Somewhere, a map app whispered: recalculating... again.
So how do you cross something that big? You import camels.
At least fifteen thousand arrived, most of them from British India.
Then trucks showed up, so the camels were set free.
Today it has the world's biggest wild camel herd... and it has even shipped camels to Saudi Arabia.
But sheep farmers had a bigger enemy: dingoes.
So they built a fence. Five thousand six hundred and fourteen kilometres long. Longer than London to New York.
Fences stopped the dogs. Emus? They just walked through.
November, nineteen thirty-two. About twenty thousand emus raid the wheat farms. So Australia sends... the army.
Two machine guns. Ten thousand bullets.
Five weeks later, the soldiers went home. The emus stayed.
In Australia, the land is so big... the animals make the rules.
The emus? Undefeated since nineteen thirty-two.
So yes... you really could lose a war to a bird.
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
